name: node-proxy-portforward-get
why: Procedure C over the node proxy: a port-forward to the kubelet /portForward endpoint through nodes/proxy, recorded as verb=get (a WebSocket upgrade, or the emulation's un-upgraded probe). The audit record shows objectRef.resource=nodes and subresource=proxy -- not pods/portforward -- and the target pod trr9026-target is carried in requestURI (objectRef.name is the node). The emulation's un-upgraded GET is refused by the kubelet (code 500, Upgrade request required), but the audit record still carries the requestURI; a real WebSocket tunnel is the same get on the same requestURI with code 101.

name: node-proxy-portforward-spdy
why: The same Procedure C tunnel over the legacy SPDY transport (an HTTP POST upgrade), recorded as verb=create on nodes/proxy with the /proxy/portForward/ path. A verb=get-only rule would miss this; the rule is verb-agnostic, so the create transport fires it too (code 101, the tunnel establishes).
source: synthetic: a raw SPDY port-forward client (for example kubeletctl) POSTing /api/v1/nodes/apiserver-control-plane/proxy/portForward/default/trr9026-target?port=8080

name: node-proxy-metrics-scrape
why: a routine monitoring scrape of the kubelet /metrics endpoint through nodes/proxy: the chokepoint (nodes/proxy) holds, but the endpoint is metrics, not portForward. Flipping requestURI alone to a /proxy/portForward/ path fires the rule, so the endpoint path must be load-bearing -- high-volume metrics and stats scraping does not fire.
source: synthetic: a Prometheus node agent GET /api/v1/nodes/apiserver-control-plane/proxy/metrics

name: node-proxy-containerlogs-pod-named-portforward
why: a containerLogs read through nodes/proxy for a pod literally named portforward: the chokepoint holds, and the string portforward appears in requestURI, but the kubelet endpoint is containerLogs, not portForward, and the pod name is lowercase. The rule matches the camelCase portForward endpoint right after /proxy/ (allowing only empty or single-dot segments between), not a lowercase portforward that appears later as a pod name. Flipping requestURI to a real /proxy/portForward/ path fires it.
source: synthetic: kubectl get --raw /api/v1/nodes/apiserver-control-plane/proxy/containerLogs/default/portforward/web (reading the logs of a pod named portforward)

name: node-proxy-portforward-encoded-endpoint
why: a port-forward whose endpoint is percent-encoded (portForwar%64 decodes to portForward) through nodes/proxy: the chokepoint holds, but the raw requestURI does not carry the literal /proxy/portForward/ path, so this rule does not fire. By design, TRR9002's k8s_node_proxy_exec fires on any nodes/proxy requestURI with a percent-encoded byte (its select_path_not_normalized), so the obfuscated port-forward is still detected there; this rule owns the unencoded path (with or without empty and single-dot segments). Flipping requestURI to the decoded literal path fires this rule.
source: synthetic: a raw client GET /api/v1/nodes/apiserver-control-plane/proxy/portForwar%64/default/trr9026-target?port=80 (endpoint percent-encoded)

name: service-proxy-portforward-backend-path
why: a services/proxy request to a backend application whose own route is /portForward/: objectRef.subresource=proxy holds and requestURI carries /proxy/portForward/, but objectRef.resource is services, not nodes. Flipping objectRef.resource alone to nodes fires the rule, so the resource=nodes constraint is load-bearing and the rule does not fire on a service proxy that happens to carry a portForward path.
source: synthetic: kubectl get --raw /api/v1/namespaces/ci/services/https:devtool:443/proxy/portForward/session/42 (a dev tool backend with its own /portForward/ route)

name: node-proxy-portforward-empty-segment
why: the same Procedure C tunnel whose proxied path carries an empty segment before the endpoint (/proxy//portForward/). The API server joins the proxied path with path.Join before it sends it to the kubelet (node/rest/proxy.go, JoinPreservingTrailingSlash), which drops the empty segment, so the kubelet receives /portForward/ and the tunnel is the real one. The rule allows empty and single-dot segments between /proxy/ and portForward/, so it fires; k8s_node_proxy_exec does not match this shape.

name: node-proxy-portforward-dot-segment
why: the same Procedure C tunnel whose proxied path carries a single-dot segment before the endpoint (/proxy/./portForward/). path.Join on the API server drops the /./ segment, so the kubelet receives /portForward/ and tunnels; the raw requestURI the rule reads still holds /proxy/./portForward/. The rule allows the single-dot segment, so it fires. This is not a /../ segment, so k8s_node_proxy_exec's select_path_not_normalized does not match it -- this rule owns this shape.

name: node-proxy-logs-query-names-portforward
why: a node log query through nodes/proxy whose query string holds /proxy/portForward/ (an operator who searches node logs for earlier proxied port-forward requests): the chokepoint holds and requestURI contains /proxy/portForward/, but only after ?, and the kubelet endpoint is /logs/. The rule reads only the path part of requestURI (the text before ?), so it does not fire. Flipping requestURI to a real /proxy/portForward/ path fires it.
